records.query: Need the histopathological biopsy report of the left second toenail lesion, as it is the gold standard for confirming malignant nail tumor and definitively excluding benign nevus or onychomycosis; dermoscopic images documenting pigment pattern and border irregularity would also aid in verifying the Hutchinson sign and guiding surgical planning.

records.query: Need the complete immunohistochemical panel including Melan-A, HMB-45, and SOX10 on the nail biopsy specimen, as the current H&E with negative S100/CD34 and no melanocytic proliferation is insufficient to conclusively exclude a malignant nail tumor; also request dermoscopic images or a second pathological consultation to verify melanocytic origin and assess Hutchinson sign.

Need dermoscopic images and PAS fungal stain results of the left second toenail lesion, which are critical to confirm onychopapilloma features (e.g., subungual hyperkeratosis, splinter hemorrhages) and definitively exclude onychomycosis, complementing the histopathological evidence.

bindings.label: New pigmented lesion on left second toenail, progressively growing for 12 months
Male in his 40s, first presentation for this problem, no prior treatments attempted, lesion asymptomatic
Physical examination showed dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering full length of left second toenail with nail thickening, pigment same width throughout and extending to proximal nail fold
No other nail or skin lesions found on examination; patient otherwise well with no fevers or weight loss
Histopathology shows no melanocytic proliferation and negative S100/CD34 immunostaining
Histopathology shows bland spindle cell proliferation with epithelial invaginations and fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate
Histopathology shows intracorneal hemorrhage and hyperkeratosis
The proximal nail fold pigment extension is a pseudo-Hutchinson sign caused by subungual hemorrhage
